title: Auto-reply to IndiaMART leads within minutes
problem: IndiaMART buyers contact 5–10 suppliers at once. The first one to send a useful reply usually gets the call.
steps: Connect IndiaMART to your CRM using its built-in integration (Kylas and Zoho CRM both offer one). Keep your IndiaMART API key handy.
Write 3 reply templates: price enquiry, sample request and bulk/OEM enquiry. Ask ChatGPT to make them short, polite and WhatsApp-friendly.
Get the templates approved in your WhatsApp Business API tool (Interakt, WATI or AiSensy).
Set an automation: new IndiaMART lead → send the matching WhatsApp template with your catalogue PDF → create a follow-up task for the salesperson.
Once a week, check which template gets the most replies and improve the weaker ones.
prompt: You are the sales desk of a Mumbai tin container manufacturer. Write a 60-word WhatsApp reply to an IndiaMART buyer asking for the price of 500 ml round tins. Ask for quantity, printing requirement and delivery city. Be polite and avoid over-promising.
caution: Don't quote final prices automatically. Let the bot collect details and leave the price to a human.

title: GST purchase-invoice data entry from photos
problem: Accounts staff spend hours typing supplier bills into Tally or Excel, and the typing errors cause GST mismatches.
steps: Make one WhatsApp group or email ID (e.g. bills@) where all supplier bills are sent as photos or PDFs.
For low volumes: upload 5–10 bill photos to ChatGPT or Gemini and ask for a table of GSTIN, invoice no., date, HSN, taxable value, CGST/SGST/IGST and total.
For high volumes: set up Nanonets or Docsumo with an invoice model and have it read from that inbox automatically.
Export to Excel/CSV in the column order your Tally import (or your accountant) expects.
Check totals against the GSTR-2B download before booking, and only fix the rows that don't match.
prompt: Extract these invoices into a table with columns: Supplier name, GSTIN, Invoice no, Invoice date, HSN, Taxable value, CGST, SGST, IGST, Total. If a field is unclear, write UNCLEAR instead of guessing.
caution: AI can misread a digit. Always reconcile against GSTR-2B before filing.

title: WhatsApp order intake without chaos
problem: Orders arrive as voice notes, photos and half-messages across several staff phones, so some get missed.
steps: Move to one official WhatsApp Business API number with a shared team inbox.
Build a short bot flow: customer name → product (from a list) → quantity → delivery city → required date.
Have each completed flow add a row to a Google Sheet (natively, or through Zapier/Make).
Send an auto-confirmation with an order reference number back to the customer.
Have the dispatch team work from the sheet, not from individual chats.
prompt: Turn this WhatsApp message into a structured order (customer, item, size, qty, delivery city, date). If something is missing, list the questions I should ask: <paste message>
caution: Keep a 'talk to a person' button. Regular dealers hate being forced through a bot.

title: Daily production report in 5 minutes
problem: Supervisors write shift output on paper or WhatsApp, and the owner gets a clear picture a week late.
steps: Give supervisors one fixed format: machine, shift, product, good qty, rejects, downtime minutes, reason.
They can send a photo of the handwritten sheet or type the format into a WhatsApp group.
Paste the messages (or photos) into ChatGPT or Gemini and ask for a consolidated table and a 5-line summary.
Keep the table in one Google Sheet. Once the format is stable, automate the step with Zapier or Make.
Review the reject % and downtime reasons each morning in a 10-minute stand-up.
prompt: From these shift updates, make a table by machine with good qty, rejects, reject %, and downtime. Then give 3 bullet points on what needs attention today.
caution: AI summarises what it's given. Garbage in, garbage out, so enforce the format.

title: Polite payment follow-up reminders
problem: Outstanding payments stretch to 90+ days because nobody wants to make the awkward call.
steps: Export your receivables ageing from Tally, Zoho Books or myBillBook.
Group customers: 0–30 days (gentle), 31–60 (firm), 60+ (escalate to owner call).
Use ChatGPT to draft 3 tone-appropriate WhatsApp and email templates in English and Hindi.
Schedule reminders through your billing app's built-in reminder feature or a WhatsApp API tool.
Every Monday, review who paid, who promised and who needs a personal call.
prompt: Write a polite but firm WhatsApp payment reminder in Hindi (Roman script) and English for a dealer with ₹1,20,000 outstanding for 45 days. Include invoice numbers placeholder and UPI/bank details placeholder.
caution: Never send automated reminders to customers with an open dispute. Tag them and exclude them.

title: Quotation drafting from an enquiry
problem: Every quotation is rewritten from scratch, and terms (GST, freight, validity) are missed or inconsistent.
steps: Create a master price list and a standard terms block (GST, freight, payment, validity, MOQ) in one document.
Paste the buyer's enquiry and your price list into ChatGPT or Claude and ask for a draft quotation.
Move the final numbers into your invoicing tool (Refrens, Zoho Books or Tally) to generate the official PDF.
Save good quotations as examples. Add them to the prompt next time so the style stays consistent.
prompt: Using my price list and standard terms below, draft a quotation for this enquiry. Show item, size, qty, rate, amount, GST % and total. List any assumptions separately. <price list> <terms> <enquiry>
caution: A human must check every rate and GST %. AI can make arithmetic errors.

title: Catalogue in Hindi, Marathi and Gujarati
problem: Dealers and retailers in tier-2/3 towns prefer their own language, but translation agencies are slow.
steps: Start from a clean English catalogue with short product descriptions (under 40 words each).
Translate using Bhashini, Google Translate or an AI assistant. Ask for simple, conversational business language.
Have a native speaker on your team or a dealer review the technical terms (sizes, materials, finishes).
Use Canva to duplicate the English catalogue design and paste in each language version.
Share the PDFs on WhatsApp and pin the right language to each dealer group.
prompt: Translate these product descriptions into simple Marathi suitable for a retailer. Keep sizes, units and brand names in English.
caution: Machine translation of technical specs can be wrong. Always get a human review.

title: Product photos for IndiaMART and Amazon listings
problem: Listings with dark, cluttered phone photos get fewer enquiries.
steps: Shoot products on a plain sheet near a window with your phone. Take 3 angles per product.
Remove backgrounds in bulk with Photoroom or remove.bg.
Make white-background images for marketplaces and a few lifestyle scenes with Pebblely for social media.
Add your logo and size details as a second image in Canva.
Replace the photos on your top 20 listings first, then compare the enquiry count after 30 days.
caution: Don't let AI change the product's real shape, colour or print. Buyers will complain on delivery.

title: Hiring: job description and first screening
problem: Vague job posts attract hundreds of mismatched applicants for a machine operator or accountant role.
steps: List the must-haves: shift timing, location, salary range, experience, language and the specific machine or software.
Ask ChatGPT or Claude for a short JD in English plus a Hindi/Marathi version for shop-floor roles.
Create 5 screening questions (e.g. 'Which press machines have you run?') and add them to your job post or application form.
Paste the anonymised responses into AI and ask it to rank candidates against the must-haves, showing its reasons.
Shortlist manually and track candidates and onboarding in Keka or greytHR.
prompt: Write a job description for a CNC operator in Vasai, 2 shifts, 2+ years experience, salary range <X–Y>. Keep it under 150 words, plus 5 screening questions.
caution: Don't let AI reject candidates on its own, and remove names, photos and gender before ranking to avoid bias.

title: Dispatch and LR (lorry receipt) tracking
problem: Customers keep calling to ask 'where is my material?', and LR copies are lost in WhatsApp.
steps: Have dispatch take a photo of every LR / e-way bill and post it in one dispatch WhatsApp group or upload it to a form.
Use AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, or Nanonets for volume) to extract the LR no., transporter, vehicle no., date, consignee and packages into a sheet.
Match each row to its order or invoice number.
Auto-send the customer a WhatsApp message with the LR number, transporter contact and expected delivery date.
Review undelivered LRs older than 7 days every week.
prompt: From this LR photo, extract: LR number, transporter, vehicle number, date, from, to, consignee, number of packages, weight. Write UNCLEAR for anything you can't read.
caution: Transporter handwriting is hard to read, so verify the vehicle number before sharing it.

title: Export enquiry email replies
problem: Foreign buyers judge you by your first email. Slow or awkward English loses good enquiries.
steps: Keep a fact sheet: capacity, certifications, MOQ, Incoterms you offer, lead times, payment terms and ports.
Paste the buyer email and fact sheet into ChatGPT or Claude and ask for a concise, professional reply.
For non-English buyers, write the reply in English and then use DeepL to translate it, keeping both versions in the email.
Never send a price or delivery commitment the AI made up. Check every number yourself.
Save your best replies as templates for each kind of enquiry.
prompt: Reply to this buyer enquiry as an Indian manufacturer. Use only the facts in my fact sheet. Be concise and professional, propose a video call and ask for their target quantity and destination port.
caution: Watch for scam enquiries (odd payment requests, links). AI can't verify who a buyer is.

title: Inventory reorder alerts for raw material
problem: Production stops because tinplate, ink or cartons ran out, and nobody noticed until the day of the job.
steps: List your top 20 raw materials and packaging items with their supplier lead times.
Ask ChatGPT to suggest reorder points from 3 months of consumption data (average daily use × lead time + safety stock).
Enter the reorder levels in Zoho Inventory, Tally or a Google Sheet.
Set an alert so that when stock falls below the reorder level, the purchase manager and owner get a WhatsApp or email message.
Review the reorder levels every quarter as volumes change.
prompt: Here is 90 days of consumption and supplier lead times. Calculate a reorder point and suggested order quantity for each item, and show the formula you used.
caution: Seasonal spikes (Diwali, export season) need manual buffers, because averages hide them.
